# 1 Kings Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-the-king Solomon loved many foreign women — and-the-daughter-of Pharaoh — Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and-Hittite —

**2** from the-nations of-which YHWH said to the-sons-of Israel, "You-shall-not go among-them and-they shall-not go among-you; surely they-will-turn ʾet-your-heart after their-gods." To-them Solomon clung in-love.

**3** And-he-had wives — princesses: seven hundred; and-concubines: three hundred. And-his-wives turned ʾet-his-heart.

**4** And-it-was at-the-time-of the-old-age-of Solomon, his-wives turned ʾet-his-heart after other gods, and-his-heart was-not complete with YHWH his-God, as the-heart-of David his-father.

**5** And-Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the-goddess-of the-Sidonians, and-after Milcom, the-abomination-of the-Ammonites.

**6** And-Solomon did the-evil in-the-eyes-of YHWH, and-did-not fully-follow after YHWH, as David his-father.

**7** Then Solomon built a-high-place for-Chemosh, the-abomination-of Moab, on-the-mountain that is before Jerusalem, and-for-Molech, the-abomination-of the-sons-of Ammon.

**8** And-so he-did for-all his-foreign wives, who-burned-incense and-sacrificed to-their-gods.

**9** And-YHWH was-angry with-Solomon, for his-heart had-turned from-YHWH, the-God-of Israel, who had-appeared to-him twice,

**10** and-had-commanded-him concerning this thing, not to-go after other gods. But-he-did-not keep ʾet-what YHWH commanded.

**11** And-YHWH said to-Solomon, "Because this has-been with-you, and-you-did-not keep my-covenant and-my-statutes that I-commanded upon-you, I-will-surely tear ʾet-the-kingdom from-upon-you and-give-it to-your-servant.

**12** Only, in-your-days I-will-not do-it, for-the-sake-of David your-father. From-the-hand-of your-son I-will-tear-it.

**13** Only, ʾet-all the-kingdom I-will-not tear-away. One tribe I-will-give to-your-son, for-the-sake-of David my-servant and-for-the-sake-of Jerusalem that I-chose."

**14** And-YHWH raised-up an-adversary to-Solomon — Hadad the-Edomite. From-the-seed-of the-king he was, in-Edom.

**15** And-it-was when-David was in-Edom, when-Joab the-commander-of the-army went-up to-bury the-slain, and-he-struck every male in-Edom —

**16** for six months Joab dwelt there, and-all Israel, until he-had-cut-off every male in-Edom —

**17** and-Hadad fled, he and-certain Edomite men from-the-servants-of his-father with-him, to-go to-Egypt. And-Hadad was a-small youth.

**18** And-they-arose from-Midian and-came to-Paran, and-they-took men with-them from-Paran and-came to-Egypt, to-Pharaoh king-of Egypt, and-he-gave to-him a-house and-food he-assigned to-him and-land he-gave to-him.

**19** And-Hadad found great favor in-the-eyes-of Pharaoh, and-he-gave to-him a-wife — the-sister-of his-own-wife, the-sister-of Tahpenes the-queen.

**20** And-the-sister-of Tahpenes bore to-him ʾet-Genubath his-son, and-Tahpenes weaned-him in-the-midst-of the-house-of Pharaoh. And-Genubath was in-the-house-of Pharaoh among the-sons-of Pharaoh.

**21** And-Hadad heard in-Egypt that David had-lain-down with his-fathers and-that Joab the-commander-of the-army was-dead. And-Hadad said to-Pharaoh, "Send-me-away, and-I-will-go to my-land."

**22** And-Pharaoh said to-him, "But what are-you lacking with-me, that behold, you are-seeking to-go to your-land?" And-he-said, "Nothing, but sending you-must-send-me."

**23** And-God raised-up to-him an-adversary — Rezon son-of Eliada, who had-fled from Hadadezer king-of Zobah, his-master.

**24** And-he-gathered to-himself men and-became commander-of a-raiding-band when-David killed-them. And-they-went to-Damascus and-dwelt in-it and-reigned in-Damascus.

**25** And-he-was an-adversary to-Israel all the-days-of Solomon — and-the-evil that Hadad did — and-he-loathed Israel and-reigned over Aram.

**26** And-Jeroboam son-of Nebat, an-Ephraimite from-Zeredah — and-the-name-of his-mother was Zeruah, a-widow woman — a-servant-of Solomon, and-he-raised a-hand against the-king.

**27** And-this is the-matter why he-raised a-hand against the-king: Solomon built ʾet-the-Millo; he-closed ʾet-the-breach-of the-City-of David his-father.

**28** And-the-man Jeroboam was a-mighty-man-of valor. And-Solomon saw the-young-man that he was doing work, and-he-appointed-him over all the-forced-labor-of the-house-of Joseph.

**29** And-it-was at-that time, and-Jeroboam went-out from-Jerusalem, and-Ahijah the-Shilonite, the-prophet, found-him on-the-way, and-he was-clothed with-a-new garment. And-the-two-of-them were alone in-the-field.

**30** And-Ahijah seized the-new garment that was upon-him, and-tore-it — twelve pieces.

**31** And-he-said to-Jeroboam, "Take for-yourself ten pieces. For thus says YHWH, the-God-of Israel: 'Behold, I am-tearing the-kingdom from-the-hand-of Solomon, and-I-will-give to-you ʾet-ten tribes.

**32** And-the-one tribe will-be his, for-the-sake-of my-servant David and-for-the-sake-of Jerusalem, the-city that I-chose from-all the-tribes-of Israel.

**33** Because they-forsook-me and-bowed-down to-Ashtoreth goddess-of the-Sidonians, to-Chemosh god-of Moab, and-to-Milcom god-of the-sons-of Ammon, and-did-not walk in-my-ways, to-do the-right in-my-eyes and-my-statutes and-my-judgments, as David his-father.

**34** And-I-will-not take ʾet-all the-kingdom from-his-hand, for prince I-will-set-him all the-days-of his-life, for-the-sake-of David my-servant whom I-chose, who kept my-commandments and-my-statutes.

**35** And-I-will-take the-kingdom from-the-hand-of his-son, and-give-it to-you — ʾet-the-ten tribes.

**36** And-to-his-son I-will-give one tribe, so-that there-may-be a-lamp for-David my-servant always before-me in-Jerusalem, the-city that I-chose for-myself to-put my-name there.

**37** And-you I-will-take, and-you-will-reign over all that your-soul desires, and-you-will-be king over Israel.

**38** And-it-shall-be, if you-hear ʾet-all that I-command-you and-walk in-my-ways and-do the-right in-my-eyes, to-keep my-statutes and-my-commandments as David my-servant did, then-I-will-be with-you and-build for-you a-lasting house, as I-built for-David, and-I-will-give to-you ʾet-Israel.

**39** And-I-will-afflict ʾet-the-seed-of David because-of this — only not all the-days.'"

**40** And-Solomon sought to-kill ʾet-Jeroboam. And-Jeroboam arose and-fled to-Egypt, to Shishak king-of Egypt, and-he-was in-Egypt until the-death-of Solomon.

**41** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Solomon, and-all that he-did, and-his-wisdom — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Acts-of Solomon?

**42** And-the-days that Solomon reigned in-Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.

**43** And-Solomon lay-down with his-fathers, and-was-buried in-the-City-of David his-father. And-Rehoboam his-son reigned in-his-place.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **11:1-2 — "clung in-love"**: The same verb (davaq) used for the first marriage in Genesis 2:24 — "a man shall cling to his wife." Solomon's clinging to foreign women inverts the creation ideal.

2. **11:4 — "not complete" (שָׁלֵם)**: The irony is in the name: Solomon (Shelomoh) comes from the root meaning "complete/whole/at peace." The man whose name means wholeness becomes the man whose heart is not whole.

3. **11:7 — "on-the-mountain before Jerusalem"**: The Mount of Olives. Solomon builds shrines to foreign gods within sight of YHWH's temple. The theological provocation is spatial — idolatry facing the house of God.

4. **11:30-31 — the torn garment**: Ahijah's prophetic sign-act echoes Samuel tearing his garment before Saul (1 Sam 15:27-28). The same symbolic action — torn fabric, torn kingdom — bookends the united monarchy.

5. **11:36 — "a-lamp for-David"**: The Hebrew ner (lamp) becomes a key motif in Kings. David's line is preserved as a lamp — fragile, small, but never extinguished. The Davidic promise survives even Solomonic failure.

— EMET
